newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: SHORT-LIST APPROVED FOR TELECOM ADVISOR.
newsitem.headline: SHORT-LIST APPROVED FOR TELECOM ADVISOR.

text.p: The Lithuanian government said on Thursday that it had approved a short-list of companies to advise on the privatisation of Lithuanian Telecom.
The European affairs ministry announced on Wednesday that the search for the lead advisor had been narrowed down from the 23 companies which had applied to bid for the tender.

The government said in a statement that the short-list is comprised of the following companies: Daiwa Institute of Research, Flemings (Hansa Investments), Merrill Lynch, Nat West Markets (Simmons & Simmons), Banque Paribas (Clifford Chance), Union Bank of Switzerland (Debevoice & Plimton, and Arthur Andersen, McDermott, Will & Emery), Dresdner Kleinwort Benson, Deutsche Morgan Grenfell and Nomura, N M Rothschild & Sons Limited and Squires, Sanders & Dempsey, Creditanstalt Investment Bank AG.
The privatisation commission must still approve the list and is expected to do so at a meeting on May 19.
After the terms of reference are sent, the companies have one month to submit their bids.
The lead advisor is expected to be named in late or early July.
The government also said in a statement that it hopes to sign the final contract to privatise the phone giant before May 1 next year.
Lithuanian Telecom is one of 13 key state assets which the government has committed itself to delivering into private hands through open bids.
